fields.before: Jonah Price, a 68-year-old man, attends clinic after resolved right arm weakness six days ago. Outside brain imaging shows no infarct or hemorrhage. Two expert reviews leave a left ICA duplex report below 50% and a CTA report above 70% in disagreement; calcific blooming obscures the CTA lumen. Renal function is at baseline. Aspirin, statin therapy and risk-factor treatment have begun.

CT shows infarction and edema involving about half the left MCA territory, without hemorrhage. The hospital stroke team is providing medical treatment.

fields.before: Ruth Carter, a 70-year-old woman, attends clinic after outside assessment for a brief right-eye visual loss eight days ago. CTA shows a very tight right bulb lumen, a threadlike distal right cervical ICA, and delayed intracranial filling. The distal right ICA is smaller than both the opposite ICA and the right external carotid artery. Brain imaging shows no infarct. She has had no recurrence since starting medical prevention.

fields.before: Martin Bell, a 74-year-old man, attends clinic after another resolved episode of left-arm weakness yesterday. Four weeks earlier, a similar event led to detection of atrial fibrillation. The initial team favored cardiac embolism and started warfarin. Recorded INRs since then are 2.4, 2.6 and 2.5, with the latest drawn during yesterday's assessment. Brain MRI shows two small recent right cortical infarcts without hemorrhage or edema. CTA shows ordinary 81% right ICA stenosis with a patent normal-caliber distal vessel and a low cervical lesion. He lives independently, walks without angina or dyspnea, and has no prior neck surgery or radiation. The procedural teams meet audited guideline risk criteria. Lipid treatment and the indicated AF prevention continue under the treating teams' perioperative protocol.
